## Ruling · four additions to this epic · 2026-10-28T14:31Z

**Maintainer rulings** (objectstack session `session_01J8VVAjRKqdoEYQ4hXxtBuf`, 2026-10-28, verbatim, not translated), reached in the session thread after the seat put the four open items to the maintainer directly: 「插件应该支持从应用市场安装才是合理的」 · 「代码插件要到下次启动才加载，这个问题也要解决」 · 「好，把热加载和依赖策略并进清单」 · on the four-item table below, 「同意」. ⛔ Not a claim; the epic PM integrates these into the milestone chain. The children M4 / M5 / the SDK-contract card are filed by this seat on these rulings and name this comment.

| # | Decision | Effect on the record |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | **Plugins get an administrator shelf in the marketplace.** The consumer shelf stays Apps-only (ADR-0019 D1 unchanged); a second shelf, visible and usable only to holders of `manage_platform_settings`, lists `artifact_kind: 'plugin'` versions and installs them through the M2 path. | **ADR-0019 D2 is amended** ("plugins are never in the consumer marketplace" → "plugins are listed on the administrator shelf, never on the consumer shelf"); this epic's 「M1 is listed on no marketplace surface」 stands for M1 and is lifted by **M4**. Tier H: the ADR line is drafted by the seat that drafts the others and landed by the maintainer. |
| 2 | **Hot attach / detach without restart is a goal of this epic**, sequenced after M2 as **M5**, not injected into M1/M2. Restart stays the rule for three plugin classes: plugins that extend sign-in (the better-auth instance is built at boot), database drivers, and plugins replacing a kernel core service; they declare it and the shelf shows "restart required". | **Reverses Q8's 「hot reload retired with #12587 → boot activation」** for the general case; ADR-0025 v2 §3.5 step 7 ("On next boot") gains the M5 arm. Tier H as above. |
| 3 | **A public plugin SDK contract and an external plugin repository are committed**, between M2 and M3: the three seams external plugins need (messaging channel provider, identity-object writes, a public `PluginContext` subset), a conformance testkit, the peer-dependency build check; `objectstack-ai/plugins` as the first-party home, the narrowed DingTalk plugin (per-user push channel + user mapping, sign-in via an identity broker) as its first resident. | New child card; M3's third-party tier builds on it. |
| 4 | **Shared-environment postures never load third-party code.** `group` / `isolated` environments (the cloud console's own) install no plugin from the shelf; only an environment with a dedicated runtime does. Same shape as the credential ruling on #27230 (S1). | A ⛔ line for M3 and M4; no card. |

**Dependency policy (no new decision; acceptance additions).** Q6 stands (bundled only; native addons refused in M1). M3's publish-side scan owes three more checks, to be written into the M3 card when it is filed: an SBOM emitted by `os plugin build` and stored on the version; a licence allowlist refusing copyleft dependencies at publish (bundling is redistribution); an artifact size cap. Plugins are also told, in the author handbook, to prefer the platform's `fetch` / `crypto` over vendor SDKs.

Chain after these: M0 ✅ → M1 #27123 (in flight) → M2 #27124 → SDK contract (new) → M3 (to file) → M4 shelf (new) → M5 hot attach (new).

## Ruling · #27108 after the bridges decision · 2026-10-28T16:22Z

**Maintainer rulings** (cloud project thread, 2026-10-28, verbatim, not translated): on the decision card 「插件专题 #27108 在中转方案之后怎么处理？」 the maintainer chose 「M1 做完，其余冻结」 (16:18Z), after choosing bridges over vendor plugins for DingTalk / WeCom / Feishu (16:10Z–16:16Z thread, epic #27314). ⛔ Not a claim.

| # | Decision | Effect |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | **M1 #27123 finishes** as ruled (B′, 6467932167). | Unchanged; slice 1 in flight. |
| 2 | **Frozen:** M2 #27124, M3 #27125, M4 #27284, M5 #27285, SDK contract #27287. Unfreeze when a paying customer asks for third-party code distribution. | Each child gets a comment naming this ruling; none is dispatched. |
| 3 | **Ruling 6471792611 item 3 is withdrawn**: `plugin-dingtalk` is not the first resident of an external plugins repository. DingTalk, WeCom and Feishu go through bridges (`objectstack-ai/bridges`, epic #27314). | #27287 frozen; its DingTalk acceptance moves to the bridges epic. |
| 4 | **Hosted ObjectOS Cloud loads no code plugins** (one hosted process serves many environments' kernels — not a dedicated runtime; item 4's rule applied to hosted). Follows from 2: with M2 and M4 frozen there is no fetch or shelf path to a hosted environment; the thread's open card on this question was closed as this option on that basis, not by a separate tap. | Code plugins remain for self-hosted / Enterprise dedicated runtimes through M1. |

M1 note for slice 2: its acceptance names cloud `plugins/connector-stripe`, which is closed-source in the private cloud repository (`README.md:8`, `package.json` `"license": "UNLICENSED"`), so objectstack CI cannot build it. Use an open fixture plugin for the objectstack e2e; the Stripe e2e runs in cloud CI after the pin carries M1.

M1 note for slice 2 (Docker-deployed Enterprise): the EE image declares `VOLUME ["/data"]` with `OS_HOME=/data` (cloud `apps/objectos-ee/Dockerfile:565-585`), so a plugin installed at image build time into `<OS_HOME>/plugins/` is hidden once the volume mounts. Customers who bake plugins into a derived image (`FROM objectos-ee:x`, Kubernetes, immutable deploys) need the loader to also scan a read-only plugin directory outside `OS_HOME` (e.g. `OS_PLUGINS_DIR`), with the same signature re-verification at boot. Runtime install into the `/data` volume (`docker compose exec app os plugin install …`, then restart) works as designed.
